note: Vol. I No. 34. THE CHICAGO LETTER LIST IS WITHDRAWN this week — only the Juliet list still stands, at page 4 column 2, and it is badly cut. What this issue adds instead is the town's own economy in print: a weekly PRICES CURRENT corrected for the Democrat by P. F. Peck, a boarding school placed by a church and two streets with its fees in dollars, and a dwelling and a store offered to rent with their rooms counted. Page 3 columns 3, 4 and 5 are the Tesseract fallback and are cut down their right edge by a leading article; every supply below is bracketed.

claims.notes: THE TOWN'S PRICES, WEEKLY, AND A NAMED MERCHANT BEHIND THEM. This is the first prices current in the July run and it is signed in the head: corrected for the Democrat by P. F. Peck, the merchant at the corner of LaSalle and South Water (1834-07-02, claim c023). A commodity list with a name attached is a claim about the market AND about who in the town was trusted to state it. THE COLUMN IS CUT DOWN ITS LEFT EDGE by the leading article, so most commodity names survive only as their last letters ('exh b', 'It mess bh', '> prime') and the FIGURES survive better than the goods. Every commodity name in the normalized reading is therefore bracketed as a supply, and the four that cannot be supplied at all are left out of `lines_of_claim` rather than guessed. THE FIGURES ARE QUOTED AS PRINTED and not converted: '9 00', '5 50', '9 a 10' are dollars and cents and cents-per-pound ranges as the paper set them. A fuller witness for this table would be a later issue in which the segmenter cuts the column the other way, which is how the July run has settled every other cut so far.

claims.notes: THE SCHOOL THE MONTH HAS BEEN TRYING TO PLACE. On 1834-07-09 the same notice ran at page 3 column 1 in an interleave so bad that only 'ing a school for young', '[uncertain: ng Ladies in Bange]', 'street, hear' and 'son, church, between Cierk and' survived, and no claim was made from it. Page 3 column 3 of THIS issue reads it out at lines 3344-3348 — 'MISS BAYNE'S B[oarding School] for Young Ladie[s …] [stand]ing on Randolph Stree[t …] Presbyterian Church, be[tween Clark and Dear]born streets' — and this column repeats it with the fee table. TAKEN TOGETHER: a girls' school on Randolph Street, behind the Presbyterian Church, in the block between Clark and Dearborn, at three dollars a quarter with fancy work at five, drawing at seven and painting at eight. THE PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IS NEW TO THIS RUN and is the second church in it — the Baptist Church places Collins & Caton on South Water Street (1834-07-02, claim c016). THE PROPRIETRESS is named only in the other column, as 'MISS BAYNE'S', and is bracketed here because this claim's own lines do not carry her.

claims.notes: THREE BUILDINGS IN ONE NOTICE — a dwelling with its rooms counted, a store on South Water Street, and a small building on another street — and the whole of it is cut down the left edge by the leading article, so almost every noun is a supply. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRINTED: 'VENIENT Dwelling with', 'ome and a kitchen on', 'floor. Also, a STORE', 'Water-atreet, anc » small', 'street. Enquire of'. 'South' before 'Water-street' is supplied because South Water is the only Water street this paper names; 'Randolph' before the second 'street' is NOT supplied — the bracket in the normalized reading carries it as a guess made visible, and a reader should treat it as unread. The number of rooms is likewise a supply from 'ome', which supports 'rooms' and no particular count; '[three ro]oms' is one reading of it and the bracket says so. THIS CLAIM IS DELIBERATELY WEAK AND IS KEPT for the STORE ON SOUTH WATER STREET, which is printed in capitals and is not in doubt: a store standing empty enough to advertise, in the town's principal street, in July 1834.

claims.notes: A TRADESMAN WITH NO PREMISES OF HIS OWN, TAKING ORDERS AT ANOTHER MAN'S COUNTER — which is a different kind of business from a storefront and is worth distinguishing, because a reconstruction that gives every advertiser a building would put a shop where there was none. `placement.class` is `relative` on the store of Hubbard & Co. because that is where the work is transacted, and `street` is null because neither this notice nor any other in the July run gives Hubbard & Co. a street (see 1834-07-02, claim c045). THE REFERENCES ARE THREE OF THE TOWN'S PRINCIPAL HOUSES — Hubbard & Co., Newberry & Dole, and John H. Kinzie — named as vouchers for a new tailor, dated the day before the issue. That is a social fact as much as a commercial one. The other half of this advertisement is in page 3 column 3 at lines 3357-3368.

claims.contradicts: the partnerships Deacon & McCaleb and E. P. Deacon & Co., dissolved 16 July 1834
claims.notes: RULING 3's VETO, AND IT REACHES INTO CHICAGO. On 1834-07-02 David Carver advertised that he had 'just obtained the Agency for Messrs. Deacon & M'Cal[e]y, (proprietors of the Steam Saw Mill at St. Joseph)' and would keep pine at his Chicago lumber yard (claim c006 there, where the firm's name was read two different ways in one issue and neither was preferred). Three weeks later the firm is dissolved. `contradicts` is set on this claim, so the compiler will not stand Deacon & McCaleb in the 1835 town; CARVER'S OWN BUSINESS IS NOT CONTRADICTED — his yard is his, and only his supply is in question. THE SURNAME IS SPELLED THREE WAYS IN THIS NOTICE ALONE: 'McCaleb' at 3532, 'McKaleb' at 3538, 'McKALEB' at 3542, plus 'McCALEB' at 3553 in the succeeding notice. No merge is declared and the entity carries a bracket: a name the paper cannot spell twice the same way is not one this project should settle from OCR.

claims.notes: THE SUCCESSION HALF of claim c005's dissolution, and it is what keeps Chicago's pine coming: the LUMBER business is continued by E. P. Deacon alone at the steam mill, while the stock of goods is sold off at cost by McCaleb. So Carver's Chicago yard loses a partnership and keeps a supplier. Two businesses are compiled from these two claims — the dissolved partnership, contradicted, and E. P. Deacon's continuing mill, not contradicted — which is the shape ruling 3 is meant to produce. The year on the second dateline prints '1838' at line 3558 and is read 1834 from the issue and from the insertion code '6w34'; it is not bracketed in the entity because the reading is the paper's own arithmetic, and it is stated here. T-0694: McCaleb's entity now carries St. Joseph, the place his partner's entity on this claim already carries and the place c005's dissolution notice puts the same pair of men at in this same issue. He is the retiring partner of a St. Joseph steam mill selling off its stock, not a Chicago storefront, and reading his role as `proprietor` with no place is what would let a later pass raise one for him here.

claims.notes: THE STOVE FIRM'S ADVERTISEMENT PRINTED WHOLE, AND ITS FIRST PARTNER'S NAME CHANGES. On 1834-07-09 the same standing advertisement was cut down its left edge and signed 'M, JONES,' (claim c020 there); here it is signed 'WM. JONES,'. M. and Wm. are not the same initial, and the identity policy refuses to merge a surname across differing initials with or without a rule — so BOTH stand as entities and the business carries all three proprietor strings, which is deliberately untidy. The dateline resolves it no better: both printings date from Chicago, and this one gives 8 July while the earlier gave none. A THIRD WITNESS in a later issue is what settles it. THE STOCK LIST IS FULLER HERE than in the cut printing — Franklin and Hall stoves, chauldrons, corn cultivators — and those goods are what the business record now carries.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. The display line did not survive the interleave — line 636 reads 'all' and line 635 closes P. Pruyne & Co.'s notice above — so the card runs here from its trade line. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. 638, 639, 641 and 644 are the woven column's fragments, named in `lines` and not quoted. This is the FOURTH consecutive week to print '12 Building Lots' after 1834-07-09 printed '122': the figure the corpus can read wobbles between the two and neither is corrected against the other here.
